newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Power supply to Marcos crypt cut over unpaid bills.
newsitem.headline: Power supply to Marcos crypt cut over unpaid bills.

text.p: A power firm on Monday cut the supply of electricity to the mausoleum of of former president Ferdinand Marcos because of unpaid bills, company officials said.
The Ilocos Norte Electric Cooperative disconnected the supply to the Marcos compound in Batac town in the northern Philippines at 9.15 a.m. (0115 GMT).
Local reporters were present when workers pulled the plug on the compound where a family mansion and a library housing memorabilia of the late president also stand.
The cooperative had given the family until the close of business last Friday to pay bills which they said totalled 5.643 million pesos ($214,500).

"We waited for word from the Marcoses and gave them time to settle the account but it seems nobody would like to negotiate so we cut it off," Eduardo Arzadon, a department manager of the cooperative, told Reuters.

Members of the Marcos family in Manila were not immediately available for comment. Cooperative officials earlier said the family was questioning why the amount, which includes unpaid bills over several years, was so big.

The body of the president, who was ousted in a 1986 popular revolt and died in exile in Hawaii in 1989, has lain in the mausoleum since 1993, when President Fidel Ramos allowed the remains to be brought to the Philippines.
A Filipino embalmer has preserved the corpse with injections of chemicals.
